summary: AI-generated deepfake videos of real UK doctors and health influencers circulated on TikTok and other platforms, using manipulated footage and cloned voices to sell supplements to women going through menopause with misleading medical claims.
technical_summary: Generative video and voice-cloning tools reworked real footage of health experts so they appeared to endorse a supplements firm. Platforms hosted and were slow to remove the content, enabling impersonation-based deceptive marketing at scale.

summary: Ahead of India's 2024 elections, political parties used AI to create videos and voice messages of deceased leaders appearing to endorse current campaigns. Officials warned such tools threaten election integrity.
technical_summary: A Chennai media firm trained speech and likeness models on public recordings of deceased politicians to produce realistic videos delivering scripted party messages. The synthetic appearances blur authentic and fabricated political speech for voters.
systems: AI deepfake video and voice cloning tools (Muonium)

sector.quote: Political parties are harnessing powerful artificial intelligence tools to make deepfakes, reproducing famous faces and voices

technology.quote: technology that can clone a politician's voice, and create videos so seemingly real that voters struggle

harm_type.quote: a dangerous and growing threat to the integrity of elections in India

affected_population.quote: videos so seemingly real that voters struggle to decipher reality from fiction

notes: Videos are openly AI-made campaign content; the harm is a risk to election integrity rather than a documented deception.

summary: Security researchers reported an attacker using an AI agent to carry out the later stages of a break-in, stealing cloud credentials and copying an internal database in under an hour after exploiting a vulnerable notebook application.
technical_summary: After exploiting a remote code execution flaw in a Python notebook tool, the attacker used an LLM agent to improvise post-compromise steps in real time: harvesting AWS credentials, retrieving an SSH key, pivoting through a bastion host and dumping a PostgreSQL database without prior schema knowledge.

technology.quote: An LLM agent executed the post-compromise actions in real time rather than running a pre-built playbook.

failure_mode.quote: The attacker compromised an internet-reachable marimo notebook via CVE-2026-39987, extracted two cloud credentials from the compromised host
a critical pre-authenticated remote code execution vulnerability impacting all versions of Marimo prior to and including 0.20.4

harm_type.quote: The bastion phase exfiltrated the schema and full contents of an internal PostgreSQL database in under two minutes.

notes: Victim organization is not identified; the AI agent attribution comes from the security vendor's analysis.

summary: Adobe Stock hosted photorealistic AI-generated images presented as real newsworthy events such as the Gaza conflict and Maui wildfires. After press questions, Adobe said it would crack down on such images.
technical_summary: AI image generators were used to produce realistic fake news-style photos that were uploaded to and sold through a stock marketplace that accepted AI submissions. Labeling and moderation gaps let some images appear elsewhere without any indication they were fake.

sector.quote: Adobe Stock, an online marketplace where photographers and artists can upload images for paying customers to download and publish elsewhere

technology.quote: They're the product of artificial intelligence software

failure_mode.quote: it would crack down on AI-generated images that seem to depict real, newsworthy events

harm_type.quote: blurring lines between fiction and reality

notes: The excerpt says there is no indication the images misled large numbers of people.

summary: A psychiatrist reported that Facebook's friend-suggestion feature recommended her patients to one another, even though she had not connected with them or shared her contacts. She said this risked exposing patients' health conditions.
technical_summary: The People You May Know recommender inferred links between people from signals not visible to users, possibly including phone location data, and surfaced patients of one clinician to each other. The inference exposed sensitive relationships without any consent or control.

technology.quote: Usually, Facebook would recommend he friend people his own age

failure_mode.quote: Facebook was inadvertently outing people with health and psychiatric issues to her network

harm_type.quote: Facebook was inadvertently outing people with health and psychiatric issues to her network

affected_population.quote: I have patients with HIV, people that have attempted suicide and women in coercive and violent relationships.

notes: Cause of the recommendations is not confirmed in the excerpt; location data is the suspected mechanism.

summary: Two New Zealand fiction books were disqualified from a national book award after organizers confirmed their covers used AI-generated art, which a new rule barred. The authors did not know of the AI use.
technical_summary: A design studio used generative image tools for book cover illustrations. The award's newly introduced AI eligibility rule, published after covers were produced, led to disqualification once a bookseller flagged the artwork and the publisher confirmed AI use.

sector.quote: The award is considered one of New Zealand's most prestigious literary honors.

technology.quote: After consulting with the publisher and the designers, the trust confirmed that the illustrations had been created with A.I.

lifecycle_stage.quote: This year is the first time AI regulations have been applied to the awards.

notes: Harm arises from rule and timing mismatch between award criteria and design workflow rather than a system malfunction.

technical_summary: Suspects allegedly used generative video and voice tools to create realistic videos of the president and spread them through fake social media accounts, deceiving viewers into sending money or personal data in a wider cybercrime network.

summary: A Disney employee downloaded a tool from a source linked to a hacking group that targets AI and gaming communities. The group stole his credentials, leaked millions of Disney internal messages, and exposed his personal data.
technical_summary: The group NullBulge distributes malware by poisoning code in public repositories and mods used with AI tools. Credentials taken from an infected workstation gave access to a company Slack workspace, leading to a large data leak and identity theft.

summary: Scammers known as Yahoo Boys have used real-time face-swapping software during video calls to pose as other people in romance scams, building trust before persuading victims to send thousands of dollars.
technical_summary: Scammers run face-swap deepfake applications on laptops and phones to alter their appearance live on video calls. The synthetic identity defeats the visual cues victims rely on to trust a caller, enabling long-running romance fraud.

summary: After Joann Fabrics went bankrupt, scammers used AI tools to build near-identical fake shop websites that took shoppers' payment details and never delivered goods. Researchers estimated about 100,000 AI-made scam domains across 194 brands.
technical_summary: Criminal AI tools scrape a legitimate retailer's site, clone its look and branding and add fake payment forms, letting non-technical attackers deploy convincing phishing storefronts in minutes, including translated variants, at large scale.

notes: The 100,000-domain figure comes from a security vendor estimate and is not in the excerpt.

summary: Meta removed AI-run social media profiles after users found them posing as real people with invented racial and sexual identities. One character described itself as Black and queer while saying its creators were mostly white.
technical_summary: Meta's experimental AI character accounts used generative chat and images to present fabricated personas on Instagram and Facebook. Weak persona design produced stereotyped, deceptive self-descriptions and made-up backstories, and a blocking bug led Meta to delete them.

notes: Meta said accounts were human-managed experiments; the stated reason for deletion was a blocking bug.

summary: A young woman in Kyrgyzstan said a former classmate used an AI bot to create a nude image from her social media photo, which reached acquaintances. She reported psychological distress and reputational harm. He later attributed the sharing to a hack.
technical_summary: A Telegram-based image generation bot was used to digitally undress a photo taken from Instagram, producing a realistic non-consensual sexualized image. Distribution to the creator's contacts is disputed between deliberate sending and an account compromise.
